exceptions.reason: No app has a stylesheet of its own: each app's app.css is compiled at build time from its classes, as utilities only, against the kit's token file (wiki/stylesheets.md), so there is no styles/index.css to hold or to count. The one hand-written sheet is the CAD dev page's harness/desktop.css.
A PDF page, a page thumbnail, a signature canvas and the typed-signature preview are paper, not themed UI: they stay white in both themes, as the mark that lands in the PDF is black on white.
The slide show is a black stage with white text and white hairlines whatever the theme, as a projector shows it.
Stacking inside one page's canvas (the text layer above the bitmap), not a floating part: it sits in the page's own stacking context and never meets the kit's z scale.
Stacking inside one page's annotation layer (the layer, a delete handle and the note editor over the page's marks), not floating parts: the numbers order siblings in the page's own stacking context.
The slide rail is a role=listbox of draggable thumbnails. Base UI has no listbox that fits drag to reorder, so it stays hand-built; it keeps the arrow keys, Home and End.

A PDF's own form controls stay native: a radio group and a multiple-choice listbox (a <select multiple>, which the kit's single-choice Select does not cover) draw a field of the document, not a control of the app (Q16). Its text, checkbox and dropdown fields use the kit.
Native text, date and time inputs stay native (Q16): the browser's picker is the best one on a phone, and Base UI has none.
